meta.title: Lídia Belas — Digital Anthropology & Gender
meta.description: Lídia Belas — undergraduate in Social Sciences/UFBA, PIBIC researcher at LABHDUFBA. Research on online misogyny, digital games, gender and technology.
hero.subtitle: Undergraduate in Social Sciences · Digital Humanities researcher
about.title: About
about.bio1: I am an undergraduate student in Social Sciences at the Federal University of Bahia (UFBA), with a bachelor's degree in Anthropology. My research is situated in the field of Digital Anthropology, focusing on gender, technology, and online sociability.
about.bio2: I am a PIBIC scholarship holder at UFBA's Digital Humanities Laboratory (LABHDUFBA), where I conduct research on online misogyny in games and gamer communities, from an anthropological approach.
about.bio3: I am interested in digital cultures and communities, the forms of sociability that emerge online, and the ways gender and technology intertwine in the everyday experience of platforms and games.
research.title: Research
research.intro: My main focus currently is online misogyny in games and gamer communities, investigated through an anthropological approach that articulates digital ethnography, discourse analysis, and computational methods.
research.area1.title: Online misogyny
research.area1.desc: Forms of gender-based hostility in digital environments, with attention to discursive repertoires and exclusionary practices in games and communities.
research.area2.title: Digital games
research.area2.desc: Gamer cultures, sociability in gaming platforms, and the gender dynamics that structure the play experience.
research.area3.title: Gender and technology
research.area3.desc: Intersections between gender, technology, and digital culture, investigating how gender norms are reproduced and contested online.
research.area4.title: Digital Anthropology
research.area4.desc: Ethnographic methods applied to digital contexts, focusing on online communities, platforms, and cultural practices mediated by technology.
